First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x)-{y}^{2} & =y \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x)-{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y) \\ 3{sec}^{2}⁡(3x)-2y(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}) & =(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}3{sec}^{2}⁡(3x) & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(2y+1) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3{sec}^{2}⁡(3x)}{2y+1}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
